handbook-usage-text:
A compost bin turns food scraps and dry plant matter into fertilizer. Add perishable items together with dry grass, cattail tops, papyrus tops, or thatch. Turn the contents occasionally by sneaking and right-clicking with a shovel. A watering can helps cool the pile.

Peat bricks provide a short-lived boost. At default settings, half a stack alongside seven stacks of greens and browns boosts decomposition and heat and helps retain aeration after turning. Scale the peat down for smaller batches. A full stack adds more danger than benefit when the pile gets hot and dry. Peat decomposes quickly and leaves very little rot. Server settings can change these effects.

Once the bin contains only rot—at least 64 pieces—seal it to begin making compost.

Keep an eye on the temperature. A neglected pile can become hotter than you bargained for, so choose its surroundings carefully.
